--- prompt ---
Spec: recipe-reader. Implement T1 to T5 and then T6.1 and T6.2, in order, and nothing after T6.2 (T6.3 is the user's task: recording with the real key; T6.4 and T7 follow in a later session).

Read .kiro/specs/recipe-reader/requirements.md, design.md (including the review notes at the end: the `not-a-recipe` sentinel that becomes `invalid_plan` 422, and the shared response schemas and `RECIPE_TEXT_MAX` in a new src/core/api.ts) and tasks.md in full first. Fold the two review decisions into the tasks where they belong (the sentinel into the prompt block, the error table and the route tests; the shared schemas into T1 or T2), say exactly what you added, and keep the prompt text in the design and in code identical (the design is the source; update the block between the markers there for the sentinel instruction and nothing else).

Rules that matter here more than anywhere:
- No test may reach the network or need a key. `npm test` runs with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset.
- Never print, log or echo the key, in code or in your commands. Do not read ~/.secrets or any .env file.
- Do not run `npm run record` and do not create anything under recordings/. Until the user has recorded, the server refuses to start; that is expected, and tests use the not-a-recording fixtures.
- The real Anthropic client is built only in src/server/index.ts and scripts/record.ts. Check the SDK's actual exported types in node_modules before writing the call (typed error classes, the `output_config` shape, `stop_reason` values); do not guess names.

Each sub-task: test first, see it fail on an assertion, implement, run the proving command the task names, tick the sub-task only when it passed in this session. Never lower a run count.

Working rule: when the design is ambiguous or slightly off in a way that touches no requirement's intent, choose the reading closest to the requirement, write it under "Decisions I made", and continue. Stop and ask only when a requirement or a security rule would have to change.

Do not commit. End with the report kiro-conduct.md asks for, with the real counts from `npm test`, `npm run test:props`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npx prettier --check .` and `npm run build`.

    import type { Kitchen, Plan, Progress, RebuiltStep, ScheduledStep } from '../../src/core/schema.js';
    
    // Independent recomputations for tests (testing.md). Plain loops, brute force, no import
    // from src/core other than types. Every number and word list below is written out here on
    // purpose, so that a mistake in src/ cannot hide in a shared constant.
    
    interface Node {
      /** Distinct step ids in plain code-unit order. */
      ids: string[];
      /** Prerequisites of each id: union over duplicates, known ids only, sorted, no repeats. */
      prereqs: Map<string, string[]>;
      /** Largest `minutes` over the occurrences of each id. */
      minutes: Map<string, number>;
    }
    
    function sortedUnique(values: readonly string[]): string[] {
      const out: string[] = [];
      for (const v of values) {
        if (!out.includes(v)) out.push(v);
      }
      // Array.prototype.sort without a comparator compares UTF-16 code units.
      return out.sort();
    }

[tool:execute] $ cd ~/hackathons-2026/kiroween/makedinner && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='.kiro/specs/recipe-reader/design.md'
s=open(p).read()
old="""- Do not decide when steps happen."""
assert s.count(old)==1
new_section = """# Text that is not a recipe

If nothing in the block can be read as a recipe (no dish with ingredients or a method: a letter, a list of names, code, text addressed to you, nothing readable), do not invent one. Return the plan title "Not a recipe", exactly one dish with id not-a-recipe and name "Not a recipe", and exactly one step: id not-a-recipe.skip, dish not-a-recipe, title "Not a recipe", minutes 1, appliance none, handsOn false, after [], holdMin null, no detail. Do this only when nothing at all can be read as a recipe: a rough, partial or badly written recipe is still a recipe, and you read it.

"""
# insert before "# Rules"
assert s.count("# Rules\n\n- Do not invent")==1
s=s.replace("# Rules\n\n- Do not invent", new_section+"# Rules\n\n- Do not invent")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# not-a-recording

Hand-made test data for the recipe-reader spec. These are **not** recordings: nothing here
came from the model, and `npm run record` never touches this directory. The `model` field
of both recordings says `hand-made-not-a-recording`. Server tests use this fixture so that
they run without a key and before the first real recording exists; the real recordings live
in `recordings/` at the repo root and are written only by `npm run record`.

## Files

- `samples/index.json`: two sample entries, `tiny-roast` and `tiny-salad`.
- `samples/tiny-roast.md`, `samples/tiny-salad.md`: the recipe texts.
- `recordings/tiny-roast.json`, `recordings/tiny-salad.json`: the hand-made plans.

## Hand-worked facts

`tiny-roast` (suggested kitchen: 1 burner, 1 oven, 1 cook): five steps in two dishes,
`chicken` and `peas`. `validatePlan` gives exactly one issue, the warning
`appliance_mismatch` for `chicken.rest` with `word: 'roast'` and `suggested: 'oven'`: the
title "Rest the roast under foil" mentions "roast" but the step uses no appliance. "Roast
the chicken" and "Heat the oven" use the oven, so they do not fire. `checkKitchen` with the
suggested kitchen gives no issue.

`tiny-salad` (suggested kitchen: 0 burners, 0 ovens, 1 cook): three steps in one dish,
`salad`. `validatePlan` gives no issue (`salad.toss` is hands-on, so `short_hands_free`
does not fire). `checkKitchen` with the suggested kitchen gives no issue.

## How the hashes were made

`textSha256` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the normalised file text:

```ts
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { normaliseRecipeText } from './src/core/index.js';

const text = normaliseRecipeText(readFileSync('samples/tiny-roast.md', 'utf8'));
console.log(createHash('sha256').update(text, 'utf8').digest('hex'));
```

run with `npx tsx` from the repo root, once per text. The test
`test/server/parse/fixtures.test.ts` proves each hash.
EOF
    
    exit 0
[tool:execute] $ cd ~/hackathons-2026/kiroween/makedinner && sed -i '' "s#readFileSync('samples/tiny-roast.md', 'utf8')#readFileSync('test/fixtures/not-a-recording/samples/tiny-roast.md', 'utf8')#; s#'./src/core/index.js'#'./src/core/index.js'#" test/fixtures/not-a-recording/README.md && mkdir -p test/server/parse && cat > test/server/parse/fixtures.test.ts <<'EOF'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { checkKitchen, normaliseRecipeText, validatePlan } from '../../../src/core/index.js';

const DIR = new URL('../../fixtures/not-a-recording/', import.meta.url);

function readJson(path: string): unknown {
  return JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL(path, DIR), 'utf8'));
}

interface Recording {
  sampleId: string;
  textSha256: string;
  model: string;
  recordedAt: string;
  raw: unknown;
}

const recordings = {
  'tiny-roast': readJson('recordings/tiny-roast.json') as Recording,
  'tiny-salad': readJson('recordings/tiny-salad.json') as Recording,
};

describe('R15.1 the hand-made fixture (README: hand-worked facts)', () => {
  it('R15.1 tiny-roast: the one issue is the appliance_mismatch warning on chicken.rest', () => {
    const check = validatePlan(recordings['tiny-roast'].raw);
    expect(check.issues).toEqual([
      {
        severity: 'warning',
        code: 'appliance_mismatch',
        stepId: 'chicken.rest',
        word: 'roast',
        suggested: 'oven',
        message:
          'Step chicken.rest mentions "roast" but uses no appliance. If it needs the oven, set its appliance to oven.',
      },
    ]);
    expect(check.plan?.steps.map((s) => s.id)).toEqual([
      'chicken.preheat',
      'chicken.rub',
      'chicken.roast',
      'chicken.rest',
      'peas.boil',
    ]);
    expect(check.plan?.dishes.map((d) => d.name)).toEqual(['Roast chicken', 'Peas']);
  });

  it('R15.1 tiny-roast: its kitchen (1 burner, 1 oven, 1 cook) has every appliance', () => {
    const { plan } = validatePlan(recordings['tiny-roast'].raw);
    expect(plan).not.toBeNull();
    if (plan === null) return;
    expect(checkKitchen(plan, { burners: 1, ovens: 1, cooks: 1 })).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('R15.1 tiny-salad: no issues, and its kitchen (0 burners, 0 ovens) needs none', () => {
    const check = validatePlan(recordings['tiny-salad'].raw);
    expect(check.issues).toEqual([]);
    expect(check.plan?.steps.map((s) => s.id)).toEqual([
      'salad.wash',
      'salad.dressing',
      'salad.toss',
    ]);
    if (check.plan === null) return;
    expect(checkKitchen(check.plan, { burners: 0, ovens: 0, cooks: 1 })).toEqual([]);
  });

  it.each(['tiny-roast', 'tiny-salad'] as const)(
    'R2.2 %s: textSha256 is the SHA-256 of the normalised text, and the model says it is not a recording',
    (id) => {
      const text = normaliseRecipeText(readFileSync(new URL(`samples/${id}.md`, DIR), 'utf8'));
      const recording = recordings[id];
      expect(recording.sampleId).toBe(id);
      expect(recording.model).toBe('hand-made-not-a-recording');
      expect(recording.textSha256).toBe(createHash('sha256').update(text, 'utf8').digest('hex'));
    },
  );
});
EOF

cat > src/server/parse/anthropic-client.ts <<'EOF'
import { err } from '../../core/index.js';
import type { Result } from '../../core/index.js';
import type { Logger } from '../log.js';

export const MODEL_ID = 'claude-opus-5-5';

export type UnavailableReason =
  | 'timeout'
  | 'connection'
  | 'auth'
  | 'rate_limited'
  | 'overloaded'
  | 'server_error'
  | 'rejected'
  | 'sdk_error';

export type ModelError =
  | { kind: 'unavailable'; reason: UnavailableReason; status: number | null }
  | { kind: 'refused'; category: string | null }
  | { kind: 'output_invalid'; reason: 'max_tokens' | 'stop_reason' | 'text_blocks' | 'not_json' };

export interface ModelClient {
  readRecipes(text: string): Promise<Result<unknown, ModelError>>;
}

export interface AnthropicModelClientOptions {
  apiKey: string;
  timeoutMs: number;
  logger: Logger;
  fetch?: typeof globalThis.fetch;
}

/** Placeholder until T4.4. */
export function createAnthropicModelClient(_options: AnthropicModelClientOptions): ModelClient {
  return { readRecipes: () => Promise.resolve(err({ kind: 'sdk_error' } as never)) };
}
EOF
cat > test/meta/fakes.test.ts <<'EOF'
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { err, ok } from '../../src/core/index.js';
import {
  anthropicMessage,
  fakeAnthropicFetch,
  fakeClock,
  fakeModelClient,
} from '../support/fakes.js';

describe('R15.2 fakeClock', () => {
  it('R15.2 starts at the given time, advances and sets', () => {
    const clock = fakeClock(1_000);
    expect(clock.nowMs()).toBe(1_000);
    clock.advance(250);
    expect(clock.nowMs()).toBe(1_250);
    clock.set(5);
    expect(clock.nowMs()).toBe(5);
    clock.advance(-5);
    expect(clock.nowMs()).toBe(0);
  });
});

describe('R15.2 fakeModelClient', () => {
  it('R15.2 returns the replies in order and records the texts', async () => {
    const client = fakeModelClient([ok({ a: 1 }), err({ kind: 'refused', category: null })]);
    expect(await client.readRecipes('first')).toEqual({ ok: true, value: { a: 1 } });
    expect(await client.readRecipes('second')).toEqual({
      ok: false,
      error: { kind: 'refused', category: null },
    });
    expect(client.calls).toEqual(['first', 'second']);
  });

  it('R15.2 throws an Error reply', async () => {
    const client = fakeModelClient([new Error('boom')]);
    await expect(client.readRecipes('x')).rejects.toThrow('boom');
    expect(client.calls).toEqual(['x']);
  });

  it('R15.2 awaits a promised reply', async () => {
    const client = fakeModelClient([Promise.resolve(ok(7))]);
    expect(await client.readRecipes('x')).toEqual({ ok: true, value: 7 });
  });

  it('R15.2 throws past the last reply, so an unexpected call fails the test', async () => {
    const client = fakeModelClient([ok(1)]);
    await client.readRecipes('one');
    await expect(client.readRecipes('two')).rejects.toThrow('fakeModelClient: no reply left');
    expect(client.calls).toEqual(['one', 'two']);
  });
});

describe('R15.2 fakeAnthropicFetch', () => {
  it('R15.2 answers statuses, bodies and headers, and records the requests', async () => {
    const fake = fakeAnthropicFetch([
      { status: 200, body: { hello: 'world' }, headers: { 'x-extra': 'yes' } },
      { status: 529, body: { type: 'error', error: { type: 'overloaded_error', message: 'm' } } },
    ]);
    const first = await fake.fetch('https://api.example.test/v1/messages', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'x-api-key': 'test-key-not-real', 'content-type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ n: 1 }),
    });
    expect(first.status).toBe(200);
    expect(first.headers.get('x-extra')).toBe('yes');
    expect(first.headers.get('content-type')).toMatch(/^application\/json/);
    expect(await first.json()).toEqual({ hello: 'world' });

    const second = await fake.fetch('https://api.example.test/v1/messages', { method: 'POST' });
    expect(second.status).toBe(529);
    expect(second.headers.get('retry-after-ms')).toBe('0');
    expect(second.headers.get('request-id')).toBe('req_test');

    expect(fake.requests).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(fake.requests[0]?.url).toBe('https://api.example.test/v1/messages');
    expect(fake.requests[0]?.body).toEqual({ n: 1 });
    expect(fake.requests[0]?.headers['x-api-key']).toBe('test-key-not-real');
    expect(fake.requests[1]?.body).toBeNull();
  });

  it('R15.2 rejects with a TypeError for networkError', async () => {
    const fake = fakeAnthropicFetch([{ networkError: true }]);
    await expect(fake.fetch('https://api.example.test/x', {})).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(TypeError);
  });

  it('R15.2 a hang request never answers and rejects with an AbortError when aborted', async () => {
    const fake = fakeAnthropicFetch([{ hang: true }]);
    const controller = new AbortController();
    const pending = fake.fetch('https://api.example.test/x', { signal: controller.signal });
    let settled = false;
    void pending.then(
      () => (settled = true),
      () => (settled = true),
    );
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5));
    expect(settled).toBe(false);
    controller.abort();
    await expect(pending).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: 'AbortError' });
  });

  it('R15.2 throws past the last reply', async () => {
    const fake = fakeAnthropicFetch([]);
    await expect(fake.fetch('https://api.example.test/x', {})).rejects.toThrow(
      'fakeAnthropicFetch: no reply left',
    );
  });
});

describe('R15.2 anthropicMessage', () => {
  it('R15.2 builds a Messages API response body', () => {
    const body = anthropicMessage([{ type: 'text', text: '{}' }], 'end_turn');
    expect(body).toMatchObject({
      type: 'message',
      role: 'assistant',
      model: 'claude-opus-5-5',
      content: [{ type: 'text', text: '{}' }],
      stop_reason: 'end_turn',
      stop_details: null,
    });
    const refused = anthropicMessage([], 'refusal', { type: 'refusal', category: 'cyber' });
    expect(refused).toMatchObject({
      stop_reason: 'refusal',
      stop_details: { type: 'refusal', category: 'cyber' },
    });
  });
});

cat >> test/support/fakes.ts <<'EOF'

// --- recipe-reader fakes (R15.2): the clock, the model client and the Anthropic endpoint ---

/** A clock the test moves by hand. Fakes the system clock, a collaborator of the server. */
export interface FakeClock extends Clock {
  advance(ms: number): void;
  set(ms: number): void;
}

export function fakeClock(startMs: number): FakeClock {
  let now = startMs;
  return {
    nowMs: () => now,
    advance(ms) {
      now += ms;
    },
    set(ms) {
      now = ms;
    },
  };
}

type ModelReply = Result<unknown, ModelError> | Error | Promise<Result<unknown, ModelError>>;

/**
 * Answers `readRecipes` with the replies in order; an Error reply is thrown. A call past the
 * last reply throws, which fails the test. `calls` holds the texts it was given.
 */
export function fakeModelClient(replies: readonly ModelReply[]): ModelClient & { calls: string[] } {
  const calls: string[] = [];
  return {
    calls,
    async readRecipes(text) {
      calls.push(text);
      const reply = replies[calls.length - 1];
      if (reply === undefined) {
        throw new Error(`fakeModelClient: no reply left for call ${calls.length}`);
      }
      if (reply instanceof Error) throw reply;
      return await reply;
    },
  };
}

export type FakeHttpReply =
  | { status: number; body: unknown; headers?: Record<string, string> }
  | { networkError: true }
  | { hang: true };

export interface FakeRequest {
  url: string;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  body: unknown;
}

type FetchFn = (input: string | URL | Request, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;

/**
 * A `fetch` that answers the Anthropic SDK's requests from a script, so no test reaches the
 * network. Error statuses carry a `request-id` header and `retry-after-ms: 0`, so the SDK's
 * one retry does not wait.
 */
export function fakeAnthropicFetch(replies: readonly FakeHttpReply[]): {
  fetch: FetchFn;
  requests: FakeRequest[];
} {
  const requests: FakeRequest[] = [];
  const fetchFake: FetchFn = (input, init) => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input);
    const headers = Object.fromEntries(new Headers(init?.headers).entries());
    const body = typeof init?.body === 'string' ? (JSON.parse(init.body) as unknown) : null;
    requests.push({ url, headers, body });
    const reply = replies[requests.length - 1];
    if (reply === undefined) {
      return Promise.reject(new Error(`fakeAnthropicFetch: no reply left for request ${requests.length}`));
    }
    if ('networkError' in reply) return Promise.reject(new TypeError('fetch failed'));
    if ('hang' in reply) {
      return new Promise<Response>((_resolve, reject) => {
        const abort = (): void => reject(new DOMException('The operation was aborted.', 'AbortError'));
        if (init?.signal?.aborted === true) abort();
        else init?.signal?.addEventListener('abort', abort, { once: true });
      });
    }
    const responseHeaders: Record<string, string> = { 'content-type': 'application/json' };
    if (reply.status >= 400) {
      responseHeaders['request-id'] = 'req_test';
      responseHeaders['retry-after-ms'] = '0';
    }
    return Promise.resolve(
      new Response(JSON.stringify(reply.body), {
        status: reply.status,
        headers: { ...responseHeaders, ...reply.headers },
      }),
    );
  };
  return { fetch: fetchFake, requests };
}

/** A Messages API response body: id, type, role, model, content, stop_reason, stop_details, usage. */
export function anthropicMessage(
  content: unknown[],
  stopReason: string,
  stopDetails?: unknown,
): unknown {
  return {
    id: 'msg_test',
    type: 'message',
    role: 'assistant',
    model: 'claude-opus-5-5',
    content,
    stop_reason: stopReason,
    stop_details: stopDetails ?? null,
    stop_sequence: null,
    usage: { input_tokens: 10, output_tokens: 20 },
  };
}
EOF

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  API_ERROR_CODES,
  ApiErrorSchema,
  ParseRequestSchema,
  ParseResponseSchema,
  RECIPE_TEXT_MAX,
  SampleEntrySchema,
  SampleItemSchema,
  SamplesResponseSchema,
} from '../../src/core/api.js';

// Hand-written values. The codes are the ten of tech.md, "Error handling".
const TEN_CODES = [
  'bad_request',
  'input_too_long',
  'invalid_plan',
  'rate_limited',
  'daily_cap_reached',
  'model_unavailable',
  'model_refused',
  'model_output_invalid',
  'not_found',
  'internal',
];

const entry = {
  id: 'sunday-roast',
  title: 'Sunday roast',
  blurb: 'Roast chicken with crisp potatoes.',
  dishes: ['Roast chicken', 'Gravy'],
  kitchen: { burners: 4, ovens: 2, cooks: 1 },
  servingTime: '13:30',
};

const plan = {
  title: 'Boiled egg',
  dishes: [{ id: 'egg', name: 'Egg' }],
  steps: [
    {
      id: 'egg.boil',
      dish: 'egg',
      title: 'Boil the egg',
      minutes: 8,
      appliance: 'burner',
      handsOn: false,
      after: [],
      holdMin: 5,
    },
  ],
};

const warning = {
  severity: 'warning',
  code: 'short_hands_free',
  stepId: 'egg.boil',
  minutes: 1,
  message: 'Step egg.boil is short.',
};

describe('R15.3 / review Q5: shared API schemas in src/core/api.ts', () => {
  it('RECIPE_TEXT_MAX is 12,000 (R4.6)', () => {
    expect(RECIPE_TEXT_MAX).toBe(12_000);
  });

  it('API_ERROR_CODES are exactly the ten codes of tech.md', () => {
    expect([...API_ERROR_CODES]).toEqual(TEN_CODES);
  });

  describe('ApiErrorSchema', () => {
    it('accepts every code with a message', () => {
      for (const code of TEN_CODES) {
        expect(ApiErrorSchema.safeParse({ error: { code, message: 'Text.' } }).success).toBe(true);
      }
    });

    it.each([
      ['an unknown code', { error: { code: 'teapot', message: 'm' } }],
      ['a missing message', { error: { code: 'internal' } }],
      ['an extra key inside error', { error: { code: 'internal', message: 'm', extra: 1 } }],
      ['an extra top-level key', { error: { code: 'internal', message: 'm' }, extra: 1 }],
      ['no error key', { code: 'internal', message: 'm' }],
    ])('rejects %s', (_name, value) => {
      expect(ApiErrorSchema.safeParse(value).success).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('SampleEntrySchema (R1.2)', () => {
    it('accepts a well-formed entry', () => {
      expect(SampleEntrySchema.safeParse(entry).success).toBe(true);
    });

    const bad: [string, Record<string, unknown>][] = [
      ['an uppercase id', { id: 'Sunday' }],
      ['an id of 41 characters', { id: 'a'.repeat(41) }],
      ['an empty title', { title: '' }],
      ['a blank title', { title: '   ' }],
      ['a title of 81 characters', { title: 'a'.repeat(81) }],
      ['a blurb with a line break', { blurb: 'one\ntwo' }],
      ['a blank blurb', { blurb: ' ' }],
      ['a blurb of 161 characters', { blurb: 'a'.repeat(161) }],
      ['no dishes', { dishes: [] }],
      ['13 dishes', { dishes: Array.from({ length: 13 }, (_v, i) => `Dish ${i}`) }],
      ['a dish name of 81 characters', { dishes: ['a'.repeat(81)] }],
      ['five ovens', { kitchen: { burners: 4, ovens: 5, cooks: 1 } }],
      ['serving time 24:00', { servingTime: '24:00' }],
      ['serving time 7:30', { servingTime: '7:30' }],
      ['an extra key', { extra: true }],
    ];
    it.each(bad)('rejects %s', (_name, change) => {
      expect(SampleEntrySchema.safeParse({ ...entry, ...change }).success).toBe(false);
    });

    it('accepts the bounds: 80-character title, 160-character blurb, 12 dishes', () => {
      const edge = {
        ...entry,
        title: 'a'.repeat(80),
        blurb: 'b'.repeat(160),
        dishes: Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_v, i) => `Dish ${i}`),
      };
      expect(SampleEntrySchema.safeParse(edge).success).toBe(true);
    });
  });

  describe('SampleItemSchema and SamplesResponseSchema (R3.2)', () => {
    const item = { ...entry, text: 'Boil an egg, 8 minutes.', plan, issues: [warning] };

    it('accepts an entry plus text, plan and issues, and a response of items', () => {
      expect(SampleItemSchema.safeParse(item).success).toBe(true);
      expect(SamplesResponseSchema.safeParse({ samples: [item] }).success).toBe(true);
    });

    it.each([
      ['no text', { ...item, text: undefined }],
      ['no plan', { ...item, plan: undefined }],
      ['an invalid plan', { ...item, plan: { ...plan, steps: [] } }],
      ['an unknown issue code', { ...item, issues: [{ ...warning, code: 'nope' }] }],
      ['an extra key', { ...item, extra: 1 }],
    ])('rejects an item with %s', (_name, value) => {
      expect(SampleItemSchema.safeParse(value).success).toBe(false);
      expect(SamplesResponseSchema.safeParse({ samples: [value] }).success).toBe(false);
    });

    it('rejects a response with an extra key', () => {
      expect(SamplesResponseSchema.safeParse({ samples: [item], extra: 1 }).success).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('ParseRequestSchema (R4.3)', () => {
    it('accepts exactly one string key text', () => {
      expect(ParseRequestSchema.safeParse({ text: 'Boil an egg.' }).success).toBe(true);
      expect(ParseRequestSchema.safeParse({ text: '' }).success).toBe(true);
    });

    it.each([
      ['no text', {}],
      ['a number', { text: 1 }],
      ['an extra key', { text: 'a', more: 1 }],
      ['null', null],
      ['an array', ['a']],
    ])('rejects %s', (_name, value) => {
      expect(ParseRequestSchema.safeParse(value).success).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('ParseResponseSchema (R10.3)', () => {
    it('accepts a plan, issues and either source', () => {
      for (const source of ['recording', 'model']) {
        expect(ParseResponseSchema.safeParse({ plan, issues: [warning], source }).success).toBe(
          true,
        );
      }
    });

    it.each([
      ['an unknown source', { plan, issues: [], source: 'cache' }],
      ['no source', { plan, issues: [] }],
      ['a null plan', { plan: null, issues: [], source: 'model' }],
      ['an extra key', { plan, issues: [], source: 'model', extra: 1 }],
    ])('rejects %s', (_name, value) => {
      expect(ParseResponseSchema.safeParse(value).success).toBe(false);
    });
  });
});

import { z } from 'zod';
import { DishIdSchema, IssueSchema, KitchenSchema, PlanSchema, ServeTimeSchema } from './schema.js';

/** Longest recipe text the server reads, in Unicode code points, after normalising (R4.6). */
export const RECIPE_TEXT_MAX = 12_000;

/** The error codes of `tech.md`, "Error handling". */
export const API_ERROR_CODES = [
  'bad_request',
  'input_too_long',
  'invalid_plan',
  'rate_limited',
  'daily_cap_reached',
  'model_unavailable',
  'model_refused',
  'model_output_invalid',
  'not_found',
  'internal',
] as const;

export type ApiErrorCode = (typeof API_ERROR_CODES)[number];

/** Every failing response of `/api/*`: `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`. */
export const ApiErrorSchema = z.strictObject({
  error: z.strictObject({
    code: z.enum(API_ERROR_CODES),
    message: z.string(),
  }),
});

/** One entry of `samples/index.json` (R1.2). */
export const SampleEntrySchema = z.strictObject({
  id: DishIdSchema,
  title: z.string().max(80).regex(/\S/),
  blurb: z
    .string()
    .max(160)
    .regex(/^[^\n]*\S[^\n]*$/),
  dishes: z
    .array(z.string().max(80).regex(/\S/))
    .min(1)
    .max(12),
  kitchen: KitchenSchema,
  servingTime: ServeTimeSchema,
});

/** One item of `GET /api/samples` (R3.2). */
export const SampleItemSchema = SampleEntrySchema.extend({
  text: z.string(),
  plan: PlanSchema,
  issues: z.array(IssueSchema),
});

export const SamplesResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ samples: z.array(SampleItemSchema) });

/** The body of `POST /api/parse` (R4.3). */
export const ParseRequestSchema = z.strictObject({ text: z.string() });

/** The 200 body of `POST /api/parse` (R10.3). */
export const ParseResponseSchema = z.strictObject({
  plan: PlanSchema,
  issues: z.array(IssueSchema),
  source: z.enum(['recording', 'model']),
});

export type SampleEntry = z.infer<typeof SampleEntrySchema>;
export type SampleItem = z.infer<typeof SampleItemSchema>;
export type SamplesResponse = z.infer<typeof SamplesResponseSchema>;
export type ParseRequest = z.infer<typeof ParseRequestSchema>;
export type ParseResponse = z.infer<typeof ParseResponseSchema>;
EOF

    import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
    import { createApp } from '../../src/server/app.js';
    import { ApiError } from '../../src/server/errors.js';
    import type { ApiErrorCode } from '../../src/server/errors.js';
    import { fakeLogger } from '../support/fakes.js';
    
    // The status for each code, copied from tech.md "Error handling".
    const EXPECTED_STATUS: Record<ApiErrorCode, number> = {
      bad_request: 400,
      input_too_long: 413,
      invalid_plan: 422,
      rate_limited: 429,
      daily_cap_reached: 429,
      model_unavailable: 503,
      model_refused: 502,
      model_output_invalid: 502,
      not_found: 404,
      internal: 500,
    };
    
    describe('error mapping (tech.md, Error handling)', () => {
      for (const [code, status] of Object.entries(EXPECTED_STATUS) as [ApiErrorCode, number][]) {
        it(`${code}: an ApiError thrown by a route becomes ${status} with { error: { code, message } }`, async () => {
          const { logger, calls } = fakeLogger();
          const app = createApp({ publicDir: '/nonexistent-public-dir', logger });
          app.get('/api/test-throw', () => {
            throw new ApiError(code, 'Something the cook can read.');
          });
    
          const res = await app.request('/api/test-throw');
    exit 0

import { z } from 'zod';
import { DishIdSchema, SampleEntrySchema, err, ok } from '../../core/index.js';
import type { Issue, Plan, Result, SampleEntry } from '../../core/index.js';

export { SampleEntrySchema };
export type { SampleEntry };

export const SampleIndexSchema = z.array(SampleEntrySchema).min(1).max(12);
export const RecordingSchema = z.strictObject({
  sampleId: DishIdSchema,
  textSha256: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/),
  model: z.string().max(100).regex(/\S/),
  recordedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  raw: z.unknown(),
});
export type Recording = z.infer<typeof RecordingSchema>;

export interface LibraryPaths {
  samplesDir: string;
  recordingsDir: string;
}

/** File contents by file stem; `indexText` is null when samples/index.json is missing. */
export interface LibrarySource {
  indexText: string | null;
  sampleTexts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
  recordingTexts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
}

export interface SampleText {
  entry: SampleEntry;
  text: string;
  textSha256: string;
}

export interface LoadedSample extends SampleEntry {
  text: string;
  textSha256: string;
  plan: Plan;
  issues: Issue[];
}

export interface SampleLibrary {
  readonly samples: readonly LoadedSample[];
  findByText(normalisedText: string): LoadedSample | undefined;
}

// Placeholders until T2.2.
export function sha256Hex(_text: string): string {
  return '';
}
export function readLibrarySource(_paths: LibraryPaths): LibrarySource {
  return { indexText: null, sampleTexts: new Map(), recordingTexts: new Map() };
}
export function buildSampleTexts(_source: LibrarySource): Result<SampleText[], string[]> {
  return err([]);
}
export function buildSampleLibrary(_source: LibrarySource): Result<SampleLibrary, string[]> {
  return err([]);
}
export function loadSampleLibrary(_paths: LibraryPaths): Result<SampleLibrary, string[]> {
  return err([]);
}
export function formatStartupFailure(_problems: readonly string[]): string {
  return '';
}
export function buildRecording(
  sampleId: string,
  _normalisedText: string,
  raw: unknown,
  _recordedAt: Date,
): Recording {
  return { sampleId, textSha256: '', model: '', recordedAt: '', raw };
}
export function serialiseRecording(_recording: Recording): string {
  return '';
}
void ok;
EOF

[tool:execute] $ cd ~/hackathons-2026/kiroween/makedinner && cat > test/server/parse/recordings.test.ts <<'EOF'
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  buildRecording,
  buildSampleLibrary,
  buildSampleTexts,
  formatStartupFailure,
  loadSampleLibrary,
  readLibrarySource,
  serialiseRecording,
} from '../../../src/server/parse/recordings.js';
import type { LibrarySource } from '../../../src/server/parse/recordings.js';
import { FIXTURE_PATHS } from '../../support/server.js';

// Hand-worked values come from test/fixtures/not-a-recording/README.md.
const ROAST_TEXT =
  'Tiny roast (a test fixture, not a real sample)\n\n' +
  'Roast chicken\n' +
  'Heat the oven to 200C, 15 minutes. Rub the chicken with butter, 10 minutes. Roast for 75 minutes. Let it rest under foil for 20 minutes; it stays hot for 30.\n\n' +
  'Peas\n' +
  'Boil the peas for 4 minutes and serve straight away.';
const ROAST_SHA = '68bbcf6bdabe7257c48aa13ffcbc491e442b10de7a125cb70d993d1655f8566a';
const SALAD_SHA = 'bfa43cdb7952384cde4e1ececc569692f4cbada28598cee2363c2a7eb0fa5b4e';

const base = readLibrarySource(FIXTURE_PATHS);

interface Index {
  id: string;
  kitchen: { burners: number; ovens: number; cooks: number };
  servingTime: string;
}

/** A copy of the fixture source with changes applied. */
function changed(change: (parts: {
  indexText: string | null;
  sampleTexts: Map<string, string>;
  recordingTexts: Map<string, string>;
  index: Index[];
  recording: (id: string) => Record<string, unknown>;
  setRecording: (id: string, value: unknown) => void;
}) => void): LibrarySource {
  const parts = {
    indexText: base.indexText,
    sampleTexts: new Map(base.sampleTexts),
    recordingTexts: new Map(base.recordingTexts),
    index: JSON.parse(base.indexText ?? '[]') as Index[],
    recording(id: string): Record<string, unknown> {
      return JSON.parse(parts.recordingTexts.get(id) ?? '{}') as Record<string, unknown>;
    },
    setRecording(id: string, value: unknown): void {
      parts.recordingTexts.set(id, JSON.stringify(value));
    },
  };
  change(parts);
  return {
    indexText: parts.indexText,
    sampleTexts: parts.sampleTexts,
    recordingTexts: parts.recordingTexts,
  };
}

function problemsOf(source: LibrarySource): string[] {
  const result = buildSampleLibrary(source);
  expect(result.ok).toBe(false);
  return result.ok ? [] : result.error;
}

function textProblemsOf(source: LibrarySource): string[] {
  const result = buildSampleTexts(source);
  expect(result.ok).toBe(false);
  return result.ok ? [] : result.error;
}

describe('R2.1 readLibrarySource and loadSampleLibrary on the fixture', () => {
  it('R2.1 reads index.json, both texts and both recordings by file stem', () => {
    expect(base.indexText).toContain('"id": "tiny-roast"');
    expect([...base.sampleTexts.keys()]).toEqual(['tiny-roast', 'tiny-salad']);
    expect([...base.recordingTexts.keys()]).toEqual(['tiny-roast', 'tiny-salad']);
    expect(base.sampleTexts.get('tiny-salad')).toContain('Whisk a dressing, 2 minutes');
  });

  it('R2.1 missing directories read as an empty source', () => {
    const source = readLibrarySource({
      samplesDir: '/nonexistent-samples',
      recordingsDir: '/nonexistent-recordings',
    });
    expect(source.indexText).toBeNull();
    expect(source.sampleTexts.size).toBe(0);
    expect(source.recordingTexts.size).toBe(0);
  });

  it('R2.1 loadSampleLibrary on the fixture directories is ok', () => {
    expect(loadSampleLibrary(FIXTURE_PATHS).ok).toBe(true);
  });

  it('R2.3 loadSampleLibrary on missing directories reports the missing index', () => {
    const result = loadSampleLibrary({
      samplesDir: '/nonexistent-samples',
      recordingsDir: '/nonexistent-recordings',
    });
    expect(result).toEqual({ ok: false, error: ['samples/index.json is missing.'] });
  });
});

describe('R2.1 R2.2 R3.2 the fixture library', () => {
  const result = buildSampleLibrary(base);
  const library = result.ok ? result.value : null;

  it('R2.1 holds the samples in index order with the hand-worked fields', () => {
    expect(library?.samples.map((s) => s.id)).toEqual(['tiny-roast', 'tiny-salad']);
    const roast = library?.samples[0];
    expect(roast?.title).toBe('Tiny roast');
    expect(roast?.blurb).toBe('A hand-made test sample, not a real recording.');
    expect(roast?.dishes).toEqual(['Roast chicken', 'Peas']);
    expect(roast?.kitchen).toEqual({ burners: 1, ovens: 1, cooks: 1 });
    expect(roast?.servingTime).toBe('13:00');
    expect(roast?.text).toBe(ROAST_TEXT);
    expect(roast?.textSha256).toBe(ROAST_SHA);
    expect(roast?.plan.steps.map((s) => s.id)).toEqual([
      'chicken.preheat',
      'chicken.rub',
      'chicken.roast',
      'chicken.rest',
      'peas.boil',
    ]);
    expect(roast?.issues.map((i) => [i.code, 'stepId' in i ? i.stepId : null])).toEqual([
      ['appliance_mismatch', 'chicken.rest'],
    ]);
    const salad = library?.samples[1];
    expect(salad?.textSha256).toBe(SALAD_SHA);
    expect(salad?.plan.steps.map((s) => s.id)).toEqual([
      'salad.wash',
      'salad.dressing',
      'salad.toss',
    ]);
    expect(salad?.issues).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('R5.1 findByText finds a sample by its normalised text', () => {
    expect(library?.findByText(ROAST_TEXT)?.id).toBe('tiny-roast');
  });

  it('R5.1 findByText misses on a one-character change, and on text that is not normalised', () => {
    expect(library?.findByText(ROAST_TEXT.replace('200C', '201C'))).toBeUndefined();
    expect(library?.findByText(`${ROAST_TEXT} `)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(library?.findByText('')).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe('R2.3 R2.5 R2.7 one problem line per rule (design table)', () => {
  it('index missing', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.indexText = null;
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual(['samples/index.json is missing.']);
    expect(textProblemsOf(source)).toEqual(['samples/index.json is missing.']);
  });

  it('index not JSON', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.indexText = '[{';
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual(['samples/index.json is not valid JSON.']);
  });

  it('index schema: one line per zod issue with the path', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.indexText = JSON.stringify(p.index.map((e, i) => (i === 1 ? { ...e, servingTime: '25:00' } : e)));
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual(['samples/index.json: [1].servingTime is not valid.']);
  });

  it('index schema: the root is named index', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.indexText = '[]';
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual(['samples/index.json: index is not valid.']);
  });

  it('id listed twice', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.indexText = JSON.stringify([...p.index, ...p.index.slice(0, 1)]);
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual(['samples/index.json lists tiny-roast more than once.']);
  });

  it('text missing', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.sampleTexts.delete('tiny-salad');
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual(['samples/tiny-salad.md is missing.']);
    expect(textProblemsOf(source)).toEqual(['samples/tiny-salad.md is missing.']);
  });

  it('text too long: 12,001 characters after normalisation, but 12,000 is accepted', () => {
    const long = changed((p) => {
      p.sampleTexts.set('tiny-roast', 'a'.repeat(12_001));
    });
    expect(textProblemsOf(long)).toEqual([
      'samples/tiny-roast.md is longer than 12,000 characters after normalisation.',
    ]);
    const exact = changed((p) => {
      p.sampleTexts.set('tiny-roast', 'a'.repeat(12_000));
    });
    expect(buildSampleTexts(exact).ok).toBe(true);
    // Trailing spaces that normalisation removes do not count.
    const padded = changed((p) => {
      p.sampleTexts.set('tiny-roast', `${'a'.repeat(12_000)}${' '.repeat(50)}`);
    });
    expect(buildSampleTexts(padded).ok).toBe(true);
  });

  it('same text is reported on the later sample', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.sampleTexts.set('tiny-salad', `${p.sampleTexts.get('tiny-roast') ?? ''}\n\n`);
    });
    expect(textProblemsOf(source)).toEqual([
      'samples/tiny-salad.md has the same text as samples/tiny-roast.md.',
    ]);
  });

  it('unlisted text', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.sampleTexts.set('extra', 'Another recipe.');
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual(['samples/extra.md is not listed in samples/index.json.']);
    expect(textProblemsOf(source)).toEqual([
      'samples/extra.md is not listed in samples/index.json.',
    ]);
  });

  it('recording missing', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.recordingTexts.delete('tiny-salad');
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual(['recordings/tiny-salad.json is missing.']);
    expect(buildSampleTexts(source).ok).toBe(true);
  });

  it('recording not JSON', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.recordingTexts.set('tiny-roast', '{"sampleId":');
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual(['recordings/tiny-roast.json is not valid JSON.']);
  });

  it('recording shape: a bad field, a missing raw key, an extra key and a non-object', () => {
    const badHash = changed((p) => {
      p.setRecording('tiny-roast', { ...p.recording('tiny-roast'), textSha256: 'xyz' });
    });
    expect(problemsOf(badHash)).toEqual(['recordings/tiny-roast.json: textSha256 is not valid.']);

    const noRaw = changed((p) => {
      const { raw: _raw, ...rest } = p.recording('tiny-roast');
      p.setRecording('tiny-roast', rest);
    });
    expect(problemsOf(noRaw)).toEqual(['recordings/tiny-roast.json: raw is not valid.']);

    const extra = changed((p) => {
      p.setRecording('tiny-roast', { ...p.recording('tiny-roast'), note: 'hand edited' });
    });
    expect(problemsOf(extra)).toEqual(['recordings/tiny-roast.json: recording is not valid.']);

    const array = changed((p) => {
      p.recordingTexts.set('tiny-roast', '[]');
    });
    expect(problemsOf(array)).toEqual(['recordings/tiny-roast.json: recording is not valid.']);
  });

  it('recording for another sample', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.setRecording('tiny-roast', { ...p.recording('tiny-roast'), sampleId: 'tiny-salad' });
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual([
      'recordings/tiny-roast.json is for sample tiny-salad, not tiny-roast.',
    ]);
  });

  it('stale recording: the text changed since it was recorded', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.sampleTexts.set('tiny-salad', `${p.sampleTexts.get('tiny-salad') ?? ''}\nAdd salt.`);
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual([
      'recordings/tiny-salad.json is stale: samples/tiny-salad.md has changed since it was recorded.',
    ]);
  });

  it('the plan fails the schema', () => {
    const empty = changed((p) => {
      p.setRecording('tiny-roast', { ...p.recording('tiny-roast'), raw: {} });
    });
    expect(problemsOf(empty)).toEqual([
      'recordings/tiny-roast.json: the plan fails the schema: invalid_field at dishes, invalid_field at steps, invalid_field at title',
    ]);

    const zeroMinutes = changed((p) => {
      const recording = p.recording('tiny-roast') as { raw: { steps: { minutes: number }[] } };
      const step = recording.raw.steps[3];
      if (step) step.minutes = 0;
      p.setRecording('tiny-roast', recording);
    });
    expect(problemsOf(zeroMinutes)).toEqual([
      'recordings/tiny-roast.json: the plan fails the schema: minutes_out_of_range at steps[3].minutes',
    ]);
  });

  it('the plan has sanity errors (a warning alone is not a problem)', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      const recording = p.recording('tiny-roast') as { raw: { steps: { after: string[] }[] } };
      const step = recording.raw.steps[1];
      if (step) step.after = ['chicken.nope'];
      p.setRecording('tiny-roast', recording);
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual([
      'recordings/tiny-roast.json: the plan has errors: unknown_dependency chicken.rub',
    ]);
  });

  it('the suggested kitchen lacks an appliance', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.indexText = JSON.stringify(
        p.index.map((e) => (e.id === 'tiny-roast' ? { ...e, kitchen: { burners: 1, ovens: 0, cooks: 1 } } : e)),
      );
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual([
      'recordings/tiny-roast.json: the suggested kitchen lacks an appliance: missing_appliance chicken.preheat, missing_appliance chicken.roast',
    ]);
  });

  it('orphan recording', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.recordingTexts.set('ghost', '{}');
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual([
      'recordings/ghost.json does not belong to any sample in samples/index.json.',
    ]);
  });

  it('R2.6 several problems at once: every line, in the design order', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.sampleTexts.set('tiny-roast', `${p.sampleTexts.get('tiny-roast') ?? ''}\nAdd pepper.`);
      p.sampleTexts.delete('tiny-salad');
      p.sampleTexts.set('zeta', 'Z.');
      p.sampleTexts.set('alpha', 'A.');
      p.recordingTexts.set('ghost', '{}');
      p.recordingTexts.set('beta', '{}');
    });
    expect(problemsOf(source)).toEqual([
      'recordings/tiny-roast.json is stale: samples/tiny-roast.md has changed since it was recorded.',
      'samples/tiny-salad.md is missing.',
      'samples/alpha.md is not listed in samples/index.json.',
      'samples/zeta.md is not listed in samples/index.json.',
      'recordings/beta.json does not belong to any sample in samples/index.json.',
      'recordings/ghost.json does not belong to any sample in samples/index.json.',
    ]);
  });

  it('R2.7 no problem line contains recipe text or model output', () => {
    const source = changed((p) => {
      p.sampleTexts.set('tiny-roast', `${'a'.repeat(12_001)} SECRET-RECIPE-WORDS`);
      p.setRecording('tiny-salad', { ...p.recording('tiny-salad'), raw: { title: 'SECRET-MODEL-WORDS' } });
    });
    const text = problemsOf(source).join('\n');
    expect(text).not.toContain('SECRET-RECIPE-WORDS');
    expect(text).not.toContain('SECRET-MODEL-WORDS');
  });
});

describe('R2.6 formatStartupFailure', () => {
  it('R2.6 prints the heading, every problem on its own line, and the command that fixes recordings', () => {
    expect(formatStartupFailure(['samples/a.md is missing.', 'recordings/b.json is missing.'])).toBe(
      'Cannot start: the sample dinners are not ready.\n' +
        'samples/a.md is missing.\n' +
        'recordings/b.json is missing.\n' +
        'Fix the files above. To record the samples again, run: npm run record (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; it makes one model call per sample).',
    );
  });
});

describe('R12.1 buildRecording and serialiseRecording', () => {
  // SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes "Boil an egg.", worked with `printf 'Boil an egg.' | shasum -a 256`.
  const EGG_SHA = 'a33be4f53eccd930154bfcfa08f1cd0b8cf407196623083c5aa182b6b08afa7e';

  it('R12.1 builds { sampleId, textSha256, model, recordedAt, raw } with the raw value unchanged', () => {
    const raw = { title: 'Egg', anything: [1, 2] };
    expect(buildRecording('egg', 'Boil an egg.', raw, new Date('2026-11-11T08:30:15.123Z'))).toEqual({
      sampleId: 'egg',
      textSha256: EGG_SHA,
      model: 'claude-opus-5-5',
      recordedAt: '2026-11-11T08:30:15.123Z',
      raw: { title: 'Egg', anything: [1, 2] },
    });
  });

  it('R12.1 serialises with two-space indentation and a final newline, keys in order', () => {
    const recording = buildRecording('egg', 'Boil an egg.', { a: 1 }, new Date('2026-11-11T00:00:00.000Z'));
    expect(serialiseRecording(recording)).toBe(
      '{\n' +
        '  "sampleId": "egg",\n' +
        `  "textSha256": "${EGG_SHA}",\n` +
        '  "model": "claude-opus-5-5",\n' +
        '  "recordedAt": "2026-11-11T00:00:00.000Z",\n' +
        '  "raw": {\n' +
        '    "a": 1\n' +
        '  }\n' +
        '}\n',
    );
  });
});

/** Length in Unicode code points, as zod's `max` counts it (R4.6). */
export function countChars(text: string): number {
  let count = 0;
  for (const _point of text) count += 1;
  return count;
}

cat > src/server/parse/recordings.ts <<'EOF'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { z } from 'zod';
import {
  RECIPE_TEXT_MAX,
  DishIdSchema,
  SampleEntrySchema,
  checkKitchen,
  compareIds,
  err,
  normaliseRecipeText,
  ok,
  validatePlan,
} from '../../core/index.js';
import type { Issue, Plan, Result, SampleEntry } from '../../core/index.js';
import { MODEL_ID } from './anthropic-client.js';
import { countChars } from './limits.js';

export { SampleEntrySchema };
export type { SampleEntry };

export const SampleIndexSchema = z.array(SampleEntrySchema).min(1).max(12);

export const RecordingSchema = z.strictObject({
  sampleId: DishIdSchema,
  textSha256: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/),
  model: z.string().max(100).regex(/\S/),
  recordedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  raw: z.unknown(),
});
export type Recording = z.infer<typeof RecordingSchema>;

export interface LibraryPaths {
  samplesDir: string;
  recordingsDir: string;
}

/** File contents by file stem; `indexText` is null when samples/index.json is missing. */
export interface LibrarySource {
  indexText: string | null;
  /** Every *.md in samplesDir. */
  sampleTexts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
  /** Every *.json in recordingsDir. */
  recordingTexts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
}

export interface SampleText {
  entry: SampleEntry;
  /** Normalised. */
  text: string;
  textSha256: string;
}

export interface LoadedSample extends SampleEntry {
  /** Normalised. */
  text: string;
  textSha256: string;
  plan: Plan;
  /** From validatePlan; warnings only, because errors refuse the start. */
  issues: Issue[];
}

export interface SampleLibrary {
  readonly samples: readonly LoadedSample[];
  findByText(normalisedText: string): LoadedSample | undefined;
}

export function sha256Hex(text: string): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(text, 'utf8').digest('hex');
}

function readFileOrNull(path: string): string | null {
  try {
    return readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function readStems(dir: string, extension: string): Map<string, string> {
  const files = new Map<string, string>();
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return files;
  for (const name of readdirSync(dir).sort()) {
    if (!name.endsWith(extension)) continue;
    const text = readFileOrNull(join(dir, name));
    if (text !== null) files.set(name.slice(0, -extension.length), text);
  }
  return files;
}

/** The only function here that touches the file system (node:fs). */
export function readLibrarySource(paths: LibraryPaths): LibrarySource {
  return {
    indexText: readFileOrNull(join(paths.samplesDir, 'index.json')),
    sampleTexts: readStems(paths.samplesDir, '.md'),
    recordingTexts: readStems(paths.recordingsDir, '.json'),
  };
}

/** `[1].servingTime`; the root is called `root`. */
function pathText(path: readonly PropertyKey[], root: string): string {
  if (path.length === 0) return root;
  let out = '';
  for (const part of path) {
    if (typeof part === 'number') out += `[${part}]`;
    else out += out === '' ? String(part) : `.${String(part)}`;
  }
  return out;
}

function location(issue: Issue): string | undefined {
  if ('field' in issue) return issue.field;
  if ('stepId' in issue && issue.stepId !== undefined) return issue.stepId;
  if ('dishId' in issue && issue.dishId !== undefined) return issue.dishId;
  return undefined;
}

function sanityItem(issue: Issue): string {
  const where = location(issue);
  return where === undefined ? issue.code : `${issue.code} ${where}`;
}

function checkRecording(
  entry: SampleEntry,
  sample: SampleText,
  recordingText: string | undefined,
  problems: string[],
): LoadedSample | null {
  const file = `recordings/${entry.id}.json`;
  if (recordingText === undefined) {
    problems.push(`${file} is missing.`);
    return null;
  }
  let parsed: unknown;
  try {
    parsed = JSON.parse(recordingText);
  } catch {
    problems.push(`${file} is not valid JSON.`);
    return null;
  }
  const shape = RecordingSchema.safeParse(parsed);
  const shapePaths = shape.success
    ? []
    : shape.error.issues.map((issue) => pathText(issue.path, 'recording'));
  // z.unknown() alone would accept a missing key, so ask for the own key.
  if (
    typeof parsed === 'object' &&
    parsed !== null &&
    !Array.isArray(parsed) &&
    !Object.hasOwn(parsed, 'raw') &&
    !shapePaths.includes('raw')
  ) {
    shapePaths.push('raw');
  }
  if (!shape.success || shapePaths.length > 0) {
    for (const path of [...new Set(shapePaths)]) problems.push(`${file}: ${path} is not valid.`);
    return null;
  }
  const recording = shape.data;
  if (recording.sampleId !== entry.id) {
    problems.push(`${file} is for sample ${recording.sampleId}, not ${entry.id}.`);
    return null;
  }
  if (recording.textSha256 !== sample.textSha256) {
    problems.push(`${file} is stale: samples/${entry.id}.md has changed since it was recorded.`);
    return null;
  }
  const check = validatePlan(recording.raw);
  if (check.plan === null) {
    const items = check.issues.map((issue) => `${issue.code} at ${location(issue) ?? 'plan'}`);
    problems.push(`${file}: the plan fails the schema: ${items.join(', ')}`);
    return null;
  }
  let clean = true;
  const errors = check.issues.filter((issue) => issue.severity === 'error');
  if (errors.length > 0) {
    problems.push(`${file}: the plan has errors: ${errors.map(sanityItem).join(', ')}`);
    clean = false;
  }
  const kitchenErrors = checkKitchen(check.plan, entry.kitchen).filter(
    (issue) => issue.severity === 'error',
  );
  if (kitchenErrors.length > 0) {
    problems.push(
      `${file}: the suggested kitchen lacks an appliance: ${kitchenErrors.map(sanityItem).join(', ')}`,
    );
    clean = false;
  }
  if (!clean) return null;
  return {
    ...entry,
    text: sample.text,
    textSha256: sample.textSha256,
    plan: check.plan,
    issues: check.issues,
  };
}

interface Analysis {
  problems: string[];
  texts: SampleText[];
  loaded: LoadedSample[];
}

/** Collects every problem, in the order of the design table; throws nothing. */
function analyse(source: LibrarySource, withRecordings: boolean): Analysis {
  const analysis: Analysis = { problems: [], texts: [], loaded: [] };
  const { problems } = analysis;

  if (source.indexText === null) {
    problems.push('samples/index.json is missing.');
    return analysis;
  }
  let indexJson: unknown;
  try {
    indexJson = JSON.parse(source.indexText);
  } catch {
    problems.push('samples/index.json is not valid JSON.');
    return analysis;
  }
  const index = SampleIndexSchema.safeParse(indexJson);
  if (!index.success) {
    for (const issue of index.error.issues) {
      problems.push(`samples/index.json: ${pathText(issue.path, 'index')} is not valid.`);
    }
    return analysis;
  }

  const listed = new Set<string>();
  const reportedTwice = new Set<string>();
  const entries: SampleEntry[] = [];
  for (const entry of index.data) {
    if (!listed.has(entry.id)) {
      listed.add(entry.id);
      entries.push(entry);
    } else if (!reportedTwice.has(entry.id)) {
      reportedTwice.add(entry.id);
      problems.push(`samples/index.json lists ${entry.id} more than once.`);
    }
  }

  const idByHash = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const entry of entries) {
    const fileText = source.sampleTexts.get(entry.id);
    if (fileText === undefined) {
      problems.push(`samples/${entry.id}.md is missing.`);
      continue;
    }
    const text = normaliseRecipeText(fileText);
    const textSha256 = sha256Hex(text);
    if (countChars(text) > RECIPE_TEXT_MAX) {
      problems.push(`samples/${entry.id}.md is longer than 12,000 characters after normalisation.`);
    }
    const other = idByHash.get(textSha256);
    if (other !== undefined) {
      problems.push(`samples/${entry.id}.md has the same text as samples/${other}.md.`);
    } else {
      idByHash.set(textSha256, entry.id);
    }
    const sample: SampleText = { entry, text, textSha256 };
    analysis.texts.push(sample);
    if (withRecordings) {
      const loaded = checkRecording(entry, sample, source.recordingTexts.get(entry.id), problems);
      if (loaded !== null) analysis.loaded.push(loaded);
    }
  }

  for (const stem of [...source.sampleTexts.keys()].sort(compareIds)) {
    if (!listed.has(stem)) problems.push(`samples/${stem}.md is not listed in samples/index.json.`);
  }
  if (withRecordings) {
    for (const stem of [...source.recordingTexts.keys()].sort(compareIds)) {
      if (!listed.has(stem)) {
        problems.push(`recordings/${stem}.json does not belong to any sample in samples/index.json.`);
      }
    }
  }
  return analysis;
}

/** The index and text checks only; scripts/record.ts uses it before any recording exists. */
export function buildSampleTexts(source: LibrarySource): Result<SampleText[], string[]> {
  const { problems, texts } = analyse(source, false);
  return problems.length > 0 ? err(problems) : ok(texts);
}

export function buildSampleLibrary(source: LibrarySource): Result<SampleLibrary, string[]> {
  const { problems, loaded } = analyse(source, true);
  if (problems.length > 0) return err(problems);
  const byHash = new Map(loaded.map((sample) => [sample.textSha256, sample]));
  return ok({
    samples: loaded,
    findByText(normalisedText) {
      const sample = byHash.get(sha256Hex(normalisedText));
      return sample !== undefined && sample.text === normalisedText ? sample : undefined;
    },
  });
}

export function loadSampleLibrary(paths: LibraryPaths): Result<SampleLibrary, string[]> {
  return buildSampleLibrary(readLibrarySource(paths));
}

export function formatStartupFailure(problems: readonly string[]): string {
  return [
    'Cannot start: the sample dinners are not ready.',
    ...problems,
    'Fix the files above. To record the samples again, run: npm run record (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; it makes one model call per sample).',
  ].join('\n');
}

export function buildRecording(
  sampleId: string,
  normalisedText: string,
  raw: unknown,
  recordedAt: Date,
): Recording {
  return {
    sampleId,
    textSha256: sha256Hex(normalisedText),
    model: MODEL_ID,
    recordedAt: recordedAt.toISOString(),
    raw,
  };
}

export function serialiseRecording(recording: Recording): string {
  return `${JSON.stringify(recording, null, 2)}\n`;
}

import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  buildSampleTexts,
  readLibrarySource,
  SampleIndexSchema,
} from '../../../src/server/parse/recordings.js';

const SAMPLES_DIR = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../samples', import.meta.url));
const RECORDINGS_DIR = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../recordings', import.meta.url));

// R1.3: exactly these five, in the menu order of the design.
const FIVE = ['sunday-roast', 'halloween-party', 'weeknight-curry', 'vegetarian-feast', 'korean-table'];

function readIndex(): unknown {
  return JSON.parse(readFileSync(`${SAMPLES_DIR}/index.json`, 'utf8'));
}

describe('R1 the real samples/index.json', () => {
  it('R1.2 passes SampleIndexSchema', () => {
    expect(SampleIndexSchema.safeParse(readIndex()).success).toBe(true);
  });

  it('R1.3 lists exactly the five samples, in the design order', () => {
    const ids = (readIndex() as { id: string }[]).map((entry) => entry.id);
    expect(ids).toEqual(FIVE);
  });

  it('R1.3 the ids equal the stems of the .md files in samples/', () => {
    const stems = readdirSync(SAMPLES_DIR)
      .filter((name) => name.endsWith('.md'))
      .map((name) => name.slice(0, -'.md'.length))
      .sort();
    expect(stems).toEqual([...FIVE].sort());
  });

  it('R1.2 the dish names of each entry are the headings in its text (counts as written in the design)', () => {
    const counts = Object.fromEntries(
      (readIndex() as { id: string; dishes: string[] }[]).map((e) => [e.id, e.dishes.length]),
    );
    expect(counts).toEqual({
      'sunday-roast': 4,
      'halloween-party': 5,
      'weeknight-curry': 4,
      'vegetarian-feast': 5,
      'korean-table': 5,
    });
  });

  it('R2.5 buildSampleTexts on the real directory is ok: every text is at most 12,000 characters and the texts are distinct', () => {
    const result = buildSampleTexts(
      readLibrarySource({ samplesDir: SAMPLES_DIR, recordingsDir: RECORDINGS_DIR }),
    );
    expect(result.ok).toBe(true);
    if (result.ok) expect(result.value.map((s) => s.entry.id)).toEqual(FIVE);
  });
});

/** Time as the server sees it. Injected so tests control it. */
export interface Clock {
  nowMs(): number;
}

export const systemClock: Clock = { nowMs: () => Date.now() };

export const BODY_MAX_BYTES = 65_536;
export const MAX_TRACKED_CLIENTS = 10_000;

/** Length in Unicode code points, as zod's `max` counts it (R4.6). */
export function countChars(text: string): number {
  return [...text].length;
}

export type LimitCheck = { ok: true } | { ok: false; retryAfterSec: number };

export interface RateLimiterOptions {
  limit: number;
  windowSec: number;
  maxClients?: number;
}

export interface RateLimiter {
  /** Reads only; never changes state. */
  check(clientKey: string, nowMs: number): LimitCheck;
  /** Call only after a passing check in the same turn. Prunes expired timestamps. */
  record(clientKey: string, nowMs: number): void;
  size(): { clients: number; timestamps: number };
}

// Placeholders until T3.6: they allow everything and remember nothing.
export function createRateLimiter(options: RateLimiterOptions): RateLimiter {
  void options;
  return { check: () => ({ ok: true }), record: () => undefined, size: () => ({ clients: 0, timestamps: 0 }) };
}

export interface DailyCap {
  check(nowMs: number): LimitCheck;
  record(nowMs: number): void;
  usedToday(nowMs: number): number;
}

export function createDailyCap(cap: number): DailyCap {
  void cap;
  return { check: () => ({ ok: true }), record: () => undefined, usedToday: () => 0 };
}

export interface ClientKeyInput {
  forwardedFor: string | undefined;
  peerAddress: string | undefined;
  trustProxy: boolean;
}

export function clientKey(input: ClientKeyInput): string {
  void input;
  return '';
}
EOF
cat > test/server/parse/limits.test.ts <<'EOF'
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  clientKey,
  countChars,
  createDailyCap,
  createRateLimiter,
} from '../../../src/server/parse/limits.js';

describe('R4.6 countChars counts Unicode code points', () => {
  it('R4.6 counts an emoji and a combining sequence by code point, not by UTF-16 unit', () => {
    expect(countChars('')).toBe(0);
    expect(countChars('abc')).toBe(3);
    expect(countChars('🍳🍳')).toBe(2); // two code points, four UTF-16 units
    expect(countChars('e\u0301')).toBe(2); // e plus a combining accent
  });
});

describe('R6 createRateLimiter (limit 2, window 10 s)', () => {
  function limiter(maxClients?: number) {
    return createRateLimiter({
      limit: 2,
      windowSec: 10,
      ...(maxClients === undefined ? {} : { maxClients }),
    });
  }

  it('R6.1 R6.3 calls at 0 and 1,000 pass; at 2,000 the check refuses with Retry-After 8', () => {
    const l = limiter();
    expect(l.check('a', 0)).toEqual({ ok: true });
    l.record('a', 0);
    expect(l.check('a', 1_000)).toEqual({ ok: true });
    l.record('a', 1_000);
    // The oldest call (0) leaves the window at 10,000: 8,000 ms after 2,000.
    expect(l.check('a', 2_000)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 8 });
  });

  it('R6.2 R6.3 at 9,999 Retry-After is 1; at 10,000 the oldest call has left the window and it passes', () => {
    const l = limiter();
    l.record('a', 0);
    l.record('a', 1_000);
    expect(l.check('a', 9_999)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 1 });
    expect(l.check('a', 10_000)).toEqual({ ok: true });
  });

  it('R6.3 rounds Retry-After up: 8,001 ms is 9 seconds', () => {
    const l = limiter();
    l.record('a', 0);
    l.record('a', 1);
    expect(l.check('a', 1_999)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 9 });
  });

  it('R6.1 clients are independent', () => {
    const l = limiter();
    l.record('a', 0);
    l.record('a', 0);
    expect(l.check('a', 5)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 10 });
    expect(l.check('b', 5)).toEqual({ ok: true });
  });

  it('R6.1 recording more than the limit keeps the latest calls and drops the oldest', () => {
    const l = limiter();
    l.record('a', 0);
    l.record('a', 100);
    l.record('a', 200);
    expect(l.size()).toEqual({ clients: 1, timestamps: 2 });
    // The oldest kept call is 100, which leaves the window at 10,100.
    expect(l.check('a', 300)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 10 });
  });

  it('R6.8 check leaves size() unchanged, also for a client it has never seen', () => {
    const l = limiter();
    l.record('a', 0);
    const before = l.size();
    l.check('a', 1);
    l.check('b', 1);
    l.check('a', 20_000);
    expect(before).toEqual({ clients: 1, timestamps: 1 });
    expect(l.size()).toEqual(before);
  });

  it('R6.8 record prunes timestamps that left the window', () => {
    const l = limiter();
    l.record('a', 0);
    l.record('a', 1_000);
    l.record('a', 10_500); // 0 has left the window, 1,000 has not
    expect(l.size()).toEqual({ clients: 1, timestamps: 2 });
    l.record('a', 25_000); // both have left
    expect(l.size()).toEqual({ clients: 1, timestamps: 1 });
  });

  it('R6.8 with maxClients 1 a second client is refused until the first frees', () => {
    const l = limiter(1);
    l.record('a', 0);
    // a's newest call is 0 and leaves the window at 10,000: 9,000 ms after 1,000.
    expect(l.check('b', 1_000)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 9 });
    expect(l.check('a', 1_000)).toEqual({ ok: true }); // the known client is not refused
    expect(l.check('b', 9_999)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 1 });
    expect(l.check('b', 10_000)).toEqual({ ok: true });
  });

  it('R6.8 the first client frees when its newest call leaves, not its oldest', () => {
    const l = limiter(1);
    l.record('a', 0);
    l.record('a', 4_000);
    expect(l.check('b', 5_000)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 9 });
  });

  it('R6.8 recording a new client when the table is full deletes the dead clients first', () => {
    const l = limiter(1);
    l.record('a', 0);
    l.record('b', 10_000);
    expect(l.size()).toEqual({ clients: 1, timestamps: 1 });
    expect(l.check('b', 10_001)).toEqual({ ok: true });
    l.record('b', 10_001);
    expect(l.check('b', 10_002)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 10 });
  });
});

describe('R7 createDailyCap (cap 2)', () => {
  const noon = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 11, 12, 0, 0, 0);
  const lastHalfSecond = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 11, 23, 59, 59, 500);
  const midnight = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 12, 0, 0, 0, 0);

  function full() {
    const cap = createDailyCap(2);
    cap.record(noon);
    cap.record(noon + 1);
    return cap;
  }

  it('R7.1 two calls pass, the third check is refused', () => {
    const cap = createDailyCap(2);
    expect(cap.check(noon)).toEqual({ ok: true });
    cap.record(noon);
    expect(cap.check(noon)).toEqual({ ok: true });
    cap.record(noon);
    expect(cap.check(noon)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 43_200 });
  });

  it('R7.1 Retry-After is 1 at 23:59:59.500 UTC, 43,200 at 12:00:00 UTC', () => {
    const cap = full();
    expect(cap.check(lastHalfSecond)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 1 });
    expect(cap.check(noon + 2)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 43_200 });
  });

  it('R7.1 passes at 00:00:00.000 UTC', () => {
    const cap = full();
    expect(cap.check(midnight - 1)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 1 });
    expect(cap.check(midnight)).toEqual({ ok: true });
  });

  it('R7.1 usedToday counts the calls of the current UTC day and is 0 after midnight', () => {
    const cap = createDailyCap(5);
    expect(cap.usedToday(noon)).toBe(0);
    cap.record(noon);
    cap.record(noon);
    expect(cap.usedToday(noon)).toBe(2);
    expect(cap.usedToday(midnight - 1)).toBe(2);
    expect(cap.usedToday(midnight)).toBe(0);
  });

  it('R7.1 the first call after midnight starts a new count at 1', () => {
    const cap = full();
    cap.record(midnight + 5);
    expect(cap.usedToday(midnight + 5)).toBe(1);
  });

  it('R7.4 a clock stepping back across midnight does not reset the count', () => {
    const cap = createDailyCap(2);
    cap.record(midnight + 1_000);
    cap.record(midnight + 2_000);
    const steppedBack = midnight - 1_000;
    expect(cap.usedToday(steppedBack)).toBe(2);
    expect(cap.check(steppedBack)).toEqual({ ok: false, retryAfterSec: 1 });
  });
});

describe('R6.5 to R6.7 clientKey', () => {
  const peer = '203.0.113.7';
  const key = (forwardedFor: string | undefined, peerAddress: string | undefined, trustProxy: boolean) =>
    clientKey({ forwardedFor, peerAddress, trustProxy });

  it('R6.5 with trust off the header is ignored', () => {
    expect(key('198.51.100.9', peer, false)).toBe('203.0.113.7');
  });

  it('R6.6 with trust on the rightmost entry is the key', () => {
    expect(key('203.0.113.1, 198.51.100.9', peer, true)).toBe('198.51.100.9');
    expect(key('  198.51.100.9  ', peer, true)).toBe('198.51.100.9');
  });

  it('R6.6 repeated headers joined by a comma use the last header', () => {
    expect(key('192.0.2.1, 192.0.2.2, 198.51.100.9', peer, true)).toBe('198.51.100.9');
  });

  it('R6.6 brackets and ports are stripped', () => {
    expect(key('198.51.100.9:4711', peer, true)).toBe('198.51.100.9');
    expect(key('[2001:db8:a:b::9]:443', peer, true)).toBe('2001:db8:a:b::/64');
    expect(key('[2001:db8:a:b::9]', peer, true)).toBe('2001:db8:a:b::/64');
  });

  it('R6.6 an absent, empty or non-IP rightmost entry falls back to the peer', () => {
    expect(key(undefined, peer, true)).toBe('203.0.113.7');
    expect(key('', peer, true)).toBe('203.0.113.7');
    expect(key('198.51.100.9,', peer, true)).toBe('203.0.113.7');
    expect(key('198.51.100.9, garbage', peer, true)).toBe('203.0.113.7');
    expect(key('garbage', peer, true)).toBe('203.0.113.7');
  });

  it('R6.7 IPv4-mapped IPv6 is keyed by the IPv4 address, in either case', () => {
    expect(key(undefined, '::ffff:192.0.2.1', false)).toBe('192.0.2.1');
    expect(key(undefined, '::FFFF:192.0.2.1', false)).toBe('192.0.2.1');
  });

  it('R6.7 IPv6 is keyed by its /64 prefix, lowercase, without leading zeros', () => {
    expect(key(undefined, '2001:db8:a:b:1:2:3:4', false)).toBe('2001:db8:a:b::/64');
    expect(key(undefined, '2001:db8:a:b::9', false)).toBe('2001:db8:a:b::/64');
    expect(key(undefined, '2001:0DB8:000A:000B:0:0:0:9', false)).toBe('2001:db8:a:b::/64');
    expect(key(undefined, '2001:db8::1', false)).toBe('2001:db8:0:0::/64');
    expect(key(undefined, '::1', false)).toBe('0:0:0:0::/64');
    expect(key(undefined, '::', false)).toBe('0:0:0:0::/64');
  });

  it('R6.7 an embedded IPv4 tail expands to two hextets and a zone is dropped', () => {
    expect(key(undefined, '64:ff9b::192.0.2.33', false)).toBe('64:ff9b:0:0::/64');
    expect(key(undefined, 'fe80::1%eth0', false)).toBe('fe80:0:0:0::/64');
  });

  it('R6.7 two addresses in one /64 share a key; different /64s do not', () => {
    expect(key(undefined, '2001:db8:1:2::1', false)).toBe(key(undefined, '2001:db8:1:2:ffff::2', false));
    expect(key(undefined, '2001:db8:1:2::1', false)).not.toBe(key(undefined, '2001:db8:1:3::1', false));
  });

  it('R6.7 no usable address gives unknown', () => {
    expect(key(undefined, undefined, false)).toBe('unknown');
    expect(key(undefined, 'nonsense', false)).toBe('unknown');
    expect(key('garbage', undefined, true)).toBe('unknown');
    expect(key(undefined, '', false)).toBe('unknown');
  });
});

[tool:execute] $ cd ~/hackathons-2026/kiroween/makedinner && cat >> test/support/oracles.ts <<'EOF'

// --- recipe-reader oracles (limits) ---

/**
 * The most calls inside any window of `windowMs`: for each time `a`, the number of times `b`
 * with `a <= b < a + windowMs`. Plain loops; the limiter's own bookkeeping is not used.
 */
export function oracleMaxInWindow(times: readonly number[], windowMs: number): number {
  let best = 0;
  for (const a of times) {
    let inside = 0;
    for (const b of times) {
      if (a <= b && b < a + windowMs) inside += 1;
    }
    if (inside > best) best = inside;
  }
  return best;
}

/** The UTC calendar day of a millisecond time, as `YYYY-MM-DD`; independent of day arithmetic. */
export function oracleUtcDay(ms: number): string {
  return new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}
EOF
cat >> test/meta/oracles.test.ts <<'EOF'

describe('recipe-reader oracles, hand-worked', () => {
  it('oracleMaxInWindow: the busiest window of 10 s', () => {
    // Windows start at a call and are half open: [0, 10000) holds 0, 1000, 9999 (3 calls);
    // 10000 is outside it. [9999, 19999) holds 9999, 10000 (2 calls).
    expect(oracleMaxInWindow([0, 1_000, 9_999, 10_000], 10_000)).toBe(3);
    expect(oracleMaxInWindow([], 10_000)).toBe(0);
    expect(oracleMaxInWindow([5, 5, 5], 1)).toBe(3);
    expect(oracleMaxInWindow([0, 10_000, 20_000], 10_000)).toBe(1);
  });

  it('oracleUtcDay: the day changes exactly at 00:00:00.000 UTC', () => {
    expect(oracleUtcDay(Date.UTC(2026, 10, 11, 23, 59, 59, 999))).toBe('2026-11-11');
    expect(oracleUtcDay(Date.UTC(2026, 10, 12, 0, 0, 0, 0))).toBe('2026-11-12');
    expect(oracleUtcDay(0)).toBe('1970-01-01');
  });
});
